1 · Field of practices

Who made it, for what venue, under which shared goals — that is the image.

Compress not the soul of the image, only its weight.

(Tao of the Image)

2 · Not a file format

JPEG and PNG are containers. They do not tell you what the image does in the world.

To choose the right format is wisdom. To not choose at all is a 5MB hero image.

(Tao of the Image)

3 · Many genres at once

Editorial, advertising, beauty, portraiture, and documentary can all be fashion photography.

Signifiers. Effective use of signifiers ensures discoverability and that the feedback is well communicated and intelligible.

(Shinkle 2008, 15)

4 · Art and commerce

Fashion images can sit in both realms at once — the boundary moves with venue and intent.

Every human being on this planet is obligated to do their best to leave this planet in better shape than we found it. Designers don’t get to opt out.

(Monteiro 2019)

5 · Read the circulation

The same picture can change when it moves from runway to retail to feed to gallery.

Whether you’re burned out, starting out, starting over, or wildly successful, the question is always the same: How to keep going?

(Kleon 2019)

Digital Creativity I · I.1 Digital images

Recall check

Alone, from memory, 3 minutes. Then compare with a partner.

  1. Shinkle lists which kinds of fashion-image practices?
  2. How does Shinkle describe the art/commerce boundary?
  3. Imagination, fantasy, creativity — identical or distinct?
  4. Where does Rubin locate taste (practitioner voice)?
  5. Lab 1 maps which four labels before file type?

Course geometric background · threshold · #c378606cc29b · Original course SVG

Timer: 3 minutes. Students answer alone, from memory, on paper; no notes, no slides.

Then 2 minutes in pairs: compare answers, then check the lesson.

Practice only: nothing is collected or graded. Five more questions with answers are on the unit practice quiz page.

Answers:

  • 1. Editorial, advertising, beauty, portraiture, documentary, among others (Shinkle 2008, 15).
  • 2. Shifting and highly permeable (Shinkle 2008, 15).
  • 3. Related but non-identical; do not collapse them (Hüppauf and Wulf 2009, 32).
  • 4. In listening and curation, not tool worship (Rubin 2023, 123).
  • 5. Practice, agents, venues, and interests (classroom habit from Shinkle 2008, 15).

Ask: Which answer could you not recall? Re-read that idea before the Lab.

Digital Creativity I · I.1 Digital images

Exercise 1 · Read one fashion photograph for the field

Choose one fashion image. Name practice, agents, venues, and interests — then say why a file type is not the answer.

The phone gives us a lot but it takes away three key elements of discovery: loneliness, uncertainty, and boredom.

(Kleon 2019)

Field map (practice · agents · venues · interests) + one container-vs-practice sentence.

Image: Miss Maquillage Digital Fashion Garment example.png

Miss Maquillage Digital Fashion Garment example · Digital fashion author / Commons upload · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

  • Timer: 15 minutes. Individual, then 3-minute pair share.
  • Choose one rights-clear or course-set fashion photograph (the image you will later use as a figurín reference).
  • Map practice / agents / venues / interests on paper or in a short note.
  • Write one sentence explaining why a container name (JPEG, RAW, PNG) is not an answer to “what kind of fashion image is this?”
  • Close: name one art/commerce tension the image carries.

Source: fashion photographs as a wide array of practices with a permeable art/commerce boundary (Shinkle 2008); steps are classroom adaptation.

Ask: Which pin on your map would change first if the image moved venue?

Digital Creativity I · I.1 Digital images

Exercise 2 · Start a digital figurín scaffold

From the image you just read, block a proportion scaffold and a simple volume figure — garment detail comes later.

A field is not a mood board — it is a map of who consecrates whom.

(Tao of the Image)

Scaffold-only export + one sentence naming the proportion decision that would survive a medium change.

Image: Barbie Dream Closet Kiosk Example Of Webcam Social Shopper.jpg

Barbie Dream Closet Kiosk Example Of Webcam Social Shopper · Unknown · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Source

  • Timer: 20 minutes. Individual. This is ACT1 craft practice, not a graded Campus Virtual submit.
  • Set a visible head-count or grid scaffold on a blank canvas.
  • Block the figure as simple volumes before any garment detail.
  • Export scaffold-only (keep a second layer or file for later finish in I.2).
  • Note one proportion decision that would survive hand → raster → vector.

Source: Classroom adaptation (figurín pedagogy sequence held — Abling page cite open).

Ask: If you deleted every “finish” stroke, would the pose still read?
